propositions: Plan review currently lacks a criterion to validate that externally-verifiable acceptance criteria are tagged with exact `[operator-attested]` and codebase-verifiable criteria are untagged or use only case-insensitive exact-match tags, allowing misclassified criteria to pass review and fail completion verification after merge.

The new evidence-kind criterion must independently classify each acceptance item and produce findings when external criteria lack the exact tag, malformed tags appear, or codebase-verifiable criteria are incorrectly tagged `[operator-attested]`.

Mixed-evidence acceptance criteria that bundle both repository proof and outside-world proof must not be silently assigned a single evidence kind; the criterion must require splitting into independently certifiable items.
High-confidence evidence-kind misclassification findings must participate in blocking plan-review policy, while deterministic keyword detection remains advisory and fail-open.

The new criterion and its evaluation must achieve 100% precision on genuine-external negatives, 100% recall on named fixture cases including A1 and 115b/8c4f, and macro precision/recall ≥0.90 across the frozen corpus without regression on previously passing fixtures.
